items.informal_name: Sum of Single-Nonzero Finite Support Function
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_8} {N : Type u_10} [inst : Zero M] [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid N] {a : α} {b : M}
  {h : α → M → N}, h a 0 = 0 → (Finsupp.single a b).sum h = h a b
items.informal_description:
If $ h(a, 0) = 0 $, then the sum of the finite support function $ f $, defined by $ f(a) = b $ and $ f(x) = 0 $ for $ x 
eq a $, under the mapping $ h $ is equal to $ h(a, b) $.

items.informal_name: Sum over Single Index in Dependent Finite Support Function
items.informal_description: For a dependent finite support function $ f $ that is non-zero only at index $ i $ with value $ b $, and a function $ h $ mapping $ (i, 0) $ to $ 0 $, the sum $ \sum_{i \in \text{supp}(f)} h(i, f(i)) $ equals $ h(i, b) $. This holds when $ \gamma $ is an additive commutative monoid and the support of $ f $ is finite.

items.informal_name: Sum of Single Basis Element in Additive Monoid Algebra
items.type:
∀ {M : Type u_2} {N : Type u_3} {R : Type u_6} [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid N] {m : M} {r : R}
  {h : M → R → N}, h m 0 = 0 → Finsupp.sum (AddMonoidAlgebra.single m r) h = h m r
items.informal_description: For any additive monoid $M$, semiring $R$, and function $h : M \times R \to N$ satisfying $h(m, 0) = 0$, the finite sum of the basis element $\text{single}_M(m, r)$ under $h$ evaluates to $h(m, r)$. This expresses that summing a formal $R$-linear combination with a single non-zero coefficient $r$ at $m$ reduces to evaluating $h$ at $(m, r)$.

items.informal_name: Sum over Finite Support Function Equals Single Term Under Non-Zero Condition
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_8} {N : Type u_10} [inst : Zero M] [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid N] {f : α →₀ M} (a : α)
  {g : α → M → N}, (∀ (b : α), f b ≠ 0 → b ≠ a → g b (f b) = 0) → (f a = 0 → g a 0 = 0) → f.sum g = g a (f a)
items.informal_description: Let $\alpha$ be a type, $M$ and $N$ be types with $M$ having a zero element and $N$ an additive commutative monoid. For a finite support function $f : \alpha \to_0 M$, an element $a \in \alpha$, and a function $g : \alpha \to M \to N$, if (1) $g(b, f(b)) = 0$ for all $b \neq a$ where $f(b) \neq 0$, and (2) $g(a, 0) = 0$ when $f(a) = 0$, then the sum $\sum_{b \in \alpha} g(b, f(b))$ equals $g(a, f(a))$.

items.informal_name: Sum of Single-Indexed Monomial in Monoid Algebra
items.type:
∀ {M : Type u_2} {N : Type u_3} {R : Type u_6} [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid N] {m : M} {r : R}
  {h : M → R → N}, h m 0 = 0 → Finsupp.sum (MonoidAlgebra.single m r) h = h m r
items.informal_description: In a monoid algebra $ R[M] $ over a semiring $ R $ and an additive commutative monoid $ M $, for any monomial $ \text{single}_m(r) $ (which has coefficient $ r $ at $ m \in M $ and zero elsewhere), and for any function $ h : M \to R \to N $ into an additive commutative monoid $ N $ satisfying $ h(m, 0) = 0 $, the sum $ \sum h(m, r) $ over the monomial equals $ h(m, r) $. This follows because all terms in the monomial vanish except at $ m $, and the zero condition ensures no contribution from zero coefficients.

items.informal_name: Sum of Finite Support Function with Indicator Equals Value at Point
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {N : Type u_16} [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid N] (f : α →₀ N) (a : α),
  (f.sum fun x v => if x = a then v else 0) = f a
items.informal_description: For a finite support function $ f : \alpha \to_0 N $ where $ N $ is an additive commutative monoid, and for any $ a : \alpha $, the sum over $ \alpha $ of $ f(x) $ multiplied by the indicator function $ \mathbf{1}_{\{a\}}(x) $ equals $ f(a) $. Formally, $ \sum_{x : \alpha} \begin{cases} f(x) & x = a \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} = f(a) $.

items.type:

  (f.sum fun x v => if a = x then v else 0) = f a
items.informal_description: For any finite support function $ f : \alpha \to₀ N $ where $ N $ is an additive commutative monoid, and for any $ a \in \alpha $, the sum $ \sum_{x \in \alpha} f(x) \cdot \mathbf{1}_{x = a} $ equals $ f(a) $.

items.informal_name: Sum of Single Functions Reconstructs Finite Support Function
items.type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_8} [inst : AddCommMonoid M] (f : α →₀ M), f.sum Finsupp.single = f
items.informal_description: For any finite support function $f : \alpha \to_0 M$ where $M$ is an additive commutative monoid, the sum of the single functions (each non-zero at one index) reconstructs $f$, i.e., $\sum_{a} \text{single}(a, f(a)) = f$.

items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2} [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : FunLike F R ℝ] (v : F) {c : ℝ} (r : R)
  [ZeroHomClass F R ℝ] [NonnegHomClass F R ℝ],

items.informal_description: For a monomial $ rX^n $ in the ring of power series over a semiring $ R $, the Gauss norm $ \|rX^n\|_{v,c} $ with respect to a valuation $ v $ and a non-negative real number $ c $ is equal to $ v(r) \cdot c^n $. This holds for any $ r \in R $, natural number $ n $, and non-negative $ c $. The Gauss norm is defined as the supremum of $ v(f_i) \cdot c^i $ over all coefficients $ f_i $ of the power series.

items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] {A : Type u_2} [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid A] {u : σ →₀ ℕ} {r : R}
  {b : (σ →₀ ℕ) → R → A}, b u 0 = 0 → Finsupp.sum ((MvPolynomial.monomial u) r) b = b u r
items.informal_description: For any additive commutative monoid $A$, commutative semiring $R$, and type $\sigma$, if $b : (\sigma \to₀ \mathbb{N}) \to R \to A$ satisfies $b(u, 0) = 0$ for a monomial $u$, then the sum of the monomial $\text{monomial}(u, r)$ over $b$ equals $b(u, r)$. This expresses that summing a single monomial term in the multivariate polynomial ring $R[\sigma]$ reduces to evaluating $b$ at the monomial's exponent vector and coefficient, provided $b$ annihilates zero coefficients.

  MvPolynomial.constantCoeff ((MvPolynomial.monomial d) r) = if d = 0 then r else 0

items.informal_name: Gauss Norm of Monomial Polynomial
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2} [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : FunLike F R ℝ] (v : F) (c : ℝ) [ZeroHomClass F R ℝ]
  (n : ℕ) (r : R), Polynomial.gaussNorm v c ((Polynomial.monomial n) r) = v r * c ^ n
items.informal_description: The Gauss norm of the monomial polynomial $ rX^n $ is equal to $ v(r) \cdot c^n $, where $ v $ is a valuation on the semiring $ R $ and $ c $ is a real number parameter.

items.informal_name: Norm of Mahler Basis Term Equals Norm of Coefficient
items.type:
∀ {p : ℕ} [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : Module ℤ_[p] E]
  [inst_2 : IsBoundedSMul ℤ_[p] E] (a : E) (n : ℕ), ‖PadicInt.mahlerTerm a n‖ = ‖a‖
items.informal_description: For the Mahler basis term function $ f(x) = a \cdot \binom{x}{n} $ in the space of continuous functions $ C(\mathbb{Z}_p, E) $, where $ E $ is a normed additive commutative group equipped with a $ \mathbb{Z}_p $-module structure, the supremum norm of $ f $ satisfies $ \|f\| = \|a\| $. Here, $ \|\cdot\| $ denotes the norm induced by the supremum of $ \|f(x)\| $ over $ x \in \mathbb{Z}_p $.

items.informal_name: Equality of Operator Norm and Coefficient Norm in Formal Multilinear Series
items.type:
∀ {𝕜 : Type u} {E : Type v} [inst : NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [inst_1 : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [inst_2 : NormedSpace 𝕜 E] {p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 𝕜 E} {n : ℕ}, ‖p n‖ = ‖p.coeff n‖
items.informal_description: For any formal multilinear series $ p $ and natural number $ n $, the operator norm of the $ n $-th term $ p_n $ is equal to the norm of the coefficient $ \text{coeff } p \, n $.

items.informal_name: Norm Equality for Scalar Terms in Formal Multilinear Series
items.type:
∀ {𝕜 : Type u_1} (E : Type u_2) [inst : NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [inst_1 : SeminormedRing E]
  [inst_2 : NormedAlgebra 𝕜 E] (c : ℕ → 𝕜) (n : ℕ) [NormOneClass E], ‖FormalMultilinearSeries.ofScalars E c n‖ = ‖c n‖
items.informal_description: For a formal multilinear series constructed from scalar coefficients $ c : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K} $ in a normed field $ \mathbb{K} $ with $ \|1\| = 1 $, the norm of the $ n $-th term is equal to the norm of the scalar $ c(n) $, i.e., $ \|\text{ofScalars}_n(c)\| = \|c(n)\| $.

items.informal_name: Gauss Norm of Monomial: $ \|rX^n\|_{v,c} = v(r) c^n $
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2} [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : FunLike F R ℝ] (v : F) {c : ℝ} (r : R)
  [ZeroHomClass F R ℝ] [NonnegHomClass F R ℝ],
  0 ≤ c → ∀ (n : ℕ), PowerSeries.gaussNorm v c ((PowerSeries.monomial n) r) = v r * c ^ n
items.informal_description: For a monomial $ rX^n $ in the ring of power series over a semiring $ R $, the Gauss norm $ \|rX^n\|_{v,c} $ with respect to a valuation $ v $ and a non-negative real number $ c $ is equal to $ v(r) \cdot c^n $. This holds for any $ r \in R $, natural number $ n $, and non-negative $ c $. The Gauss norm is defined as the supremum of $ v(f_i) \cdot c^i $ over all coefficients $ f_i $ of the power series.

items.informal_name: Mahler Measure of Constant Polynomial Equals Modulus
items.type: ∀ (z : ℂ), (Polynomial.C z).mahlerMeasure = ‖z‖
items.informal_description: For any complex number $ z $, the Mahler measure of the constant polynomial $ z $ is equal to the modulus of $ z $, i.e., $ \text{MahlerMeasure}(z) = |z| $.

items.informal_name: Norm of Single-Element Function in $ L^p $ Space Equals Element Norm
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_3} {E : α → Type u_4} {p : ENNReal} [inst : (i : α) → NormedAddCommGroup (E i)] [inst_1 : DecidableEq α],
  0 < p → ∀ (i : α) (x : E i), ‖lp.single p i x‖ = ‖x‖
items.informal_description: For any extended non-negative real number $ p $ with $ 0 < p $, index $ i $, and element $ x $ in the normed additive commutative group $ E_i $, the norm of the function in the $ L^p $ space that takes the value $ x $ at index $ i $ and zero elsewhere is equal to the norm of $ x $.

items.informal_name: Logarithmic Mahler Measure of Monomial Polynomial Equals Log of Coefficient Norm
items.type: ∀ (n : ℕ) (z : ℂ), ((Polynomial.monomial n) z).logMahlerMeasure = Real.log ‖z‖
items.informal_description: For any natural number $n$ and complex number $z$, the logarithmic Mahler measure of the monomial polynomial $zX^n$ is equal to the natural logarithm of the absolute value of $z$, i.e., $\log |z|$.
